target: Kebiasaan makan kakak sama dengan kebiasaan ayah; dua-duanya suka pedas.
english: My older sibling's eating habits are the same as father's; they both like spicy food.
tip: Dua-duanya = both of them: dua-duanya suka pedas = they both like spicy food.

target: Suasana desa ini sama tenangnya dengan desa tempat saya lahir.
english: The atmosphere of this village is as peaceful as the village where I was born.
tip: Tempat + clause = where: desa tempat saya lahir = the village where I was born.

target: Iklim di Bandung berbeda dengan iklim di Jakarta; di sana jauh lebih sejuk.
english: The climate in Bandung is different from the climate in Jakarta; it is much cooler there.
tip: Indonesian pairs 'different' with 'with', not 'from': berbeda dengan iklim di Jakarta. Berbeda dari isn't wrong, but dengan is what you'll hear.

target: Rasa mangga muda berbeda jauh dengan rasa mangga yang sudah matang.
english: The taste of an unripe mango is very different from the taste of a ripe one.
tip: Muda usually means young, but for fruit it means unripe: mangga muda = unripe mango.

target: Kopi robusta beda jauh dengan arabika; rasanya lebih pahit dan lebih kuat.
english: Robusta coffee is very different from arabica; it tastes more bitter and stronger.
tip: Beda is the everyday short form of berbeda: beda jauh = very different.

target: Desain ponsel ini mirip dengan merek sebelah, tetapi kameranya kalah jauh.
english: This phone's design is similar to the neighboring brand's, but its camera is far behind.
tip: Kalah jauh = far behind (literally loses by far): kameranya kalah jauh = its camera is far worse.

target: Kamar anak saya berantakan seperti kapal pecah.
english: My child's room is a mess, like a shipwreck.
tip: Seperti kapal pecah (like a wrecked ship) is THE image for a hopelessly messy room.

target: Siang ini panasnya seperti di dalam oven.
english: This afternoon the heat is like being inside an oven.
tip: Adding -nya makes hot into the heat: panas = hot, panasnya = the heat.

target: Kayak mimpi rasanya; tiket promo ke Jepang itu akhirnya saya dapat.
english: It feels like a dream; I finally got that promo ticket to Japan.
tip: Kayak = colloquial seperti (like); you hear it everywhere: kayak mimpi = like a dream.

target: Kopi buatan ibu pahitnya kayak obat, tetapi saya tetap minum.
english: Mom's coffee is as bitter as medicine, but I drink it anyway.
tip: Pahitnya kayak obat sounds like family chat – kayak lives in relaxed speech. The moment you write anything formal (an email, a report), it becomes seperti.

target: Dua sahabat itu ke mana-mana selalu bersama, lengket seperti perangko.
english: Those two best friends go everywhere together, stuck to each other like a stamp.
tip: Lengket seperti perangko – stuck like a stamp – is the set image for two people who are never apart. Lengket alone is the sticky feel of rice or glue.

target: Ini bakso paling enak yang pernah saya coba di kota ini.
english: This is the tastiest bakso I have ever tried in this city.
tip: Paling + yang pernah = the most ... ever: paling enak yang pernah saya coba = tastiest I ever tried.

target: Kereta pagi adalah cara paling cepat untuk sampai ke bandara.
english: The morning train is the fastest way to get to the airport.
tip: Adalah links two nouns (A is B); never use it before an adjective.

target: Kasur ini paling empuk dari semua kasur yang kami coba di toko.
english: This mattress is the softest of all the mattresses we tried in the store.
tip: Paling ... dari semua = the most ... of all: paling empuk dari semua kasur = softest of all the mattresses.

target: Nenek selalu bangun paling pagi di rumah kami.
english: Grandma always gets up the earliest in our house.
tip: Paling also works with time words: bangun paling pagi = up the earliest.

target: Harga di toko itu paling murah, tetapi antreannya juga paling panjang.
english: The prices at that store are the cheapest, but its line is also the longest.
tip: Ter- + adjective can replace paling: termurah = paling murah = the cheapest.

target: Soto di warung ini paling terkenal; turis pun rela antre satu jam.
english: The soto at this stall is the most famous; even tourists are willing to line up for an hour.
tip: Pun after a noun = even: turis pun = even tourists.

target: Saya kira restoran itu mahal, ternyata harganya cukup masuk akal.
english: I thought that restaurant was expensive; it turns out the prices are quite reasonable.
tip: Ternyata = it turns out: saya kira mahal, ternyata murah = I thought it was expensive, turns out it's cheap.

target: Paket yang saya tunggu seminggu ternyata tertinggal di kantor pos.
english: The package I waited a week for turned out to have been left behind at the post office.
tip: Ter- marks what happens with nobody intending it: tertinggal = got left behind by accident. The package ternyata tertinggal – it turned out left behind, no one chose that.

target: Dia tetap memakai jaket tebal, padahal cuaca hari ini panas sekali.
english: He still wears a thick jacket, even though the weather today is very hot.
tip: Padahal = even though / when in fact, for surprising contrast: padahal panas = even though it's hot.

target: Saya kira dia akan marah, justru dia tertawa mendengar cerita itu.
english: I thought he would be angry; on the contrary, he laughed hearing that story.
tip: Justru = actually / on the contrary, flips an expectation: justru dia tertawa = on the contrary, he laughed.

target: Jangan berangkat siang; justru pagi-pagi jalanan lebih kosong.
english: Do not leave at midday; it is actually early in the morning that the roads are emptier.
tip: Doubling a time word = really early/late: pagi-pagi = early in the morning.

target: Saya bekerja di perusahaan ini sejak tahun dua ribu dua puluh.
english: I have worked at this company since the year two thousand twenty.
tip: Sejak = since a starting point: sejak tahun lalu = since last year. The verb itself does not change.

target: Hujan turun terus sejak subuh, jadi jalanan masih basah.
english: It has been raining nonstop since dawn, so the streets are still wet.
tip: Terus after a verb = keeps on: hujan turun terus = it keeps raining.

target: Kami belum bertemu lagi sejak lulus kuliah lima tahun lalu.
english: We haven't met again since graduating from college five years ago.
tip: Sejak also takes an event: sejak lulus = since graduating, sejak menikah = since getting married.

target: Toko roti di ujung jalan itu sudah buka sejak jam enam pagi.
english: That bakery at the end of the street has been open since six this morning.
tip: Sejak marks a running start point: sudah buka sejak jam enam = open since six. Daily hours use mulai.

target: Selama musim hujan, kami jarang makan di luar rumah.
english: During the rainy season, we rarely eat outside the house.
tip: Selama + time = during/for: selama liburan = during the holiday, selama dua jam = for two hours.

target: Dia tidak boleh mengangkat barang berat selama tangannya belum sembuh.
english: He may not lift heavy things while his hand hasn't healed yet.
tip: Selama + clause = while/as long as: selama tangannya belum sembuh = while his hand isn't healed yet.

target: Sampai sekarang, kunci gudang itu belum ketemu juga.
english: Up to now, that warehouse key still hasn't turned up.
tip: Everyday speech puts the lost item in charge: kunci gudang itu belum ketemu = the warehouse key hasn't turned up. Ketemu is casual – formal writing uses ditemukan.

target: Kereta kami baru saja tiba di stasiun akhir.
english: Our train has just arrived at the final station.
tip: Baru saja + verb = just did: baru saja tiba = just arrived.
